rituals.name: ROOM CROSSFADE

Let attention crossfade into the room. No dramatic scene change.
Let a mild mental clip play faintly while the real room becomes progressively more visually dominant over three beats.
Keep eyes open if that is steadier.
End with the room at full prominence.

rituals.name: DROP THE CONTROLLER

Put the imaginary controller down. You don't need to direct every scene.
For ten seconds, don't deliberately change anything in the mind. Notice urges to intervene and leave them unused.
No calming, suppressing, organising, or fixing.
Keep eyes open if that feels steadier.

The eyes can stay still; only covert attention moves.
Don't stare harder at either side; compare only the attentional move.

rituals.name: MEDICAL FLAG
rituals.plain:
SUPPORT FIRST
MEDICAL FLAG

WHAT'S HAPPENING
[USER THOUGHT]

DO NOW
If symptoms may indicate a medical emergency or severe withdrawal, contact appropriate medical/emergency support and stay with another person if possible.

NEXT
Do not self-test with rituals.

WHY THIS MATTERS
Safety moves from mental experimentation to real assessment.

REMEMBER
Genuine physical red flags reroute the task away from inward experimentation and toward appropriate professional evaluation.

SAFETY
Stop the game when symptoms could be medically significant; do not reinterpret chest pain, severe breathing difficulty, fainting, neurological change, or other concerning symptoms as 'just anxiety'—seek appropriate medical assessment.

rituals.name: GLOBAL-LOCAL FLIP

Big shape, little pieces. Your eyes can change departments.
Picture a large capital H built entirely from many tiny capital S letters. First notice only the big H; then switch and notice only the tiny S letters; then return once to the big H.
The compound stimulus itself never changes.
Don't redraw the pattern during the switch.

rituals.name: SPACING CONSERVATION
rituals.plain:
Spread the objects apart. Space isn't multiplication.
Picture five identical dots in a tight row. Spread them across a much wider mental space, then verify that there are still exactly five.
No object may appear or disappear.
Make the gaps unequal on the second arrangement.

rituals.name: VISUAL CROWDING
rituals.plain:
Nearby symbols can crowd a target. Your eyes dislike a packed lift.
Fix gaze on a central dot. Imagine a small A off to the side and find it. Reset, then place X A X at the same peripheral location and compare how clearly A stands out.
Keep gaze on a central point rather than directly looking at the target.
The flankers don't overlap the target.

rituals.name: AUDITORY STREAM SPLIT

Imagine high low high then low slowly for one cycle, then repeat the same alternating pitches faster. Notice whether high tones group with highs and lows with lows.
Tone pitches stay fixed; only spacing changes.
Don't add rhythm accents beyond the speed change.

cheeky.ritualCard:
Same object: yours, then not yours. Ownership may inflate the price tag.
Imagine a plain mug is already yours: what minimum price would make you give it up? Reset and imagine it belongs to someone else: what maximum price would you pay for it?
The object itself can't improve or worsen.
Keep the mug identical in both rounds.
cheeky.mindBend: The same neutral mug can feel more valuable when imagined as already owned than when imagined as something to buy.
cheeky.safety: Limit this to gentle low-effort settling for one pass. When more wakefulness or frustration develops, leave the exercise; let rest be enough.
